confidence_notes: Food and drink prices come from searches of crowdsourced cost-of-living sites (MyLifeElsewhere, last updated August 2026; Expatistan; third-party sites that cite Numbeo). Those prices were in NZD and I converted them to USD at about 0.57 USD per NZD. That rate comes from the USD figures shown on MyLifeElsewhere, not from an official source. The searches found an inexpensive meal at about NZ$24.50-26.40, a cappuccino at about NZ$5.60-6.25 and a pint of beer at about NZ$11.35-12.67. For a mid-range dinner for two, sources ranged widely from about NZ$70 to NZ$165; I used NZ$140, close to the Cities Insider figure. Expatistan puts cocktails at NZ$18 but says it has only 8 data points and is not yet reliable, so I estimated about NZ$20 based on the usual premium over beer. I found no reliable Wellington average for wine by the glass; menus I could not tie to a city showed NZ$13-20, so I used about NZ$15. Accommodation figures are my own estimates from general knowledge for July, which is winter and low season in Wellington, and were not checked against any listings. The RBA figure (18 November 2026) came from a search summary that pointed to the RBA exchange-rates page; I did not open the page myself.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink are based on Wellington-specific crowdsourced data. Accommodation is benchmarked against New Zealand and Australian cities of similar size and cost, such as Christchurch, Canberra and Hobart, adjusted for Wellington's status as the capital and its quieter winter tourism.
